note:
TECHNIQUE / MEASURED -- I BROKE EVERY MERGE CANDIDATE WITH `git fetch --prune`, AND THE FIX IS QUEUED. Read this before you prune anything on lefford.

WHAT HAPPENED. My first command of the session was

  git fetch origin --prune 2>&1 | tail -2

It collected refs/remotes/origin/campaign/the-sluice: a branch merged and deleted from origin long ago, whose tracking ref survived only as local residue on this box. scripts/test-sluice.sh line 2493 hard-coded that ref. So the suite died on

  fatal: ambiguous argument 'origin/campaign/the-sluice': unknown revision or path not in the working tree

which failed the `sluice queue` suite, which failed the whole `outboard` phase, which reds EVERY candidate regardless of what it contains. campaign/the-tidemark (stage) and the astronomy census delivery (merge) both died there, ~940 s of canonical-box time each, before anyone read past the phase name.

THREE THINGS WORTH CARRYING, none of which is "be careful".

1. A REMOTE-TRACKING REF IS SHARED STATE. It lives in the common git dir, so pruning in the main checkout reaches the chamber worktree too. `--prune` reads like housekeeping and is a write to state other running jobs depend on.

2. TWO UNRELATED CANDIDATES FAILING AT THE IDENTICAL ASSERTION IS AN ENVIRONMENT SIGNAL, NOT A CODE SIGNAL. That is what identified this, and it is cheap: the phase, the assertion and the artifacts-phase rc were the same for a stage of one campaign and a merge of a completely different one. Before attributing a red to a candidate, ask what YOU changed about the box.

3. I HID IT FROM MYSELF WITH `tail -2`. The `- [deleted]` lines were in the part tail discarded; all I saw was a loose-objects warning. A truncated command output is not a result, and the truncation is most dangerous on the command you think is boring.

RECOVERY, IF YOU MEET THIS AGAIN. A deleted tracking ref for a MERGED branch is usually recoverable from the local refs/heads/ copy, which no prune touches:

  git update-ref refs/remotes/origin/campaign/the-sluice <tip-from-refs/heads>

Verify the tip is an ancestor of main before trusting it. campaign/the-cadastre then passed the exact phase that had killed the two before it, which is how the restore was confirmed rather than assumed.

BUT RESTORING IS NOT FIXING, and this is the part I want to be clear about. It returns the box to a state where the next prune breaks it again -- and where a FRESH CLONE, which never had the ref at all, reds `outboard` on day one with nothing in the tree to explain why. Same shape as the cargo-sweep dependency root CLAUDE.md already documents: a working box hiding a dependency is worse than the original gap.

THE FIX IS QUEUED as tooling/sluice-test-stable-base, 90f647901015. It anchors the fixture on origin/main -- the one remote-tracking ref this repo can assume exists, and what sluice-request.sh already defaults HV_SLUICE_BASE to. The old ref's justification (it "predates the convention") reads like a reason and is not one: the headline range is measured from HV_SLUICE_BASE to the CHILD the test mints, so the base's own trailer never mattered.

VERIFIED IN FOUR CELLS, staging the absence in a throwaway SINGLE-BRANCH CLONE rather than by deleting the real ref -- an earlier draft of the check did delete it, which would have re-broken outboard for the next chamber job, reproducing the outage by hand. The clone is also the stronger scenario: not "someone pruned" but "a box was rebuilt".

  1  worktree, new code, default base   exit 0   267 passed 0 failed
  2  FRESH CLONE, old code              exit 128 raw git fatal -- the outage
  3  FRESH CLONE, new code              exit 0   267 passed 0 failed, 0 fatals
  4  worktree, new code, bogus base     exit 1   0 fatals, named refusal

CELL 4 IS THE ONE THAT EARNED ITS KEEP, and it found a defect in my own first fix. `bad` in this suite RECORDS and RETURNS -- it does not exit -- so my guard printed its nice message and then the next line peeled `$pushed_base^{tree}` on an empty string, aborting the file under `set -u`/`set -e` with the same raw fatal I was removing, and taking the seventeen sections below it with it, including `suite: the real repository was never touched`. The shipped version mints a placeholder orphan commit so the file survives to report honestly: 267 passed, 1 failed, zero raw fatals, last section still running.

GENERAL RULE FOR THE NEXT FIXTURE REF: depend on origin/main, or MINT the ref you need and publish it yourself the way scripts/test-sluice-vet.sh does with its zz-vet-* probes. Never depend on a branch whose continued existence is somebody else's housekeeping.
